summary: Neither signal predicted the private board well. The public LB was the better sign predictor. Across 17 levers where we had an offline number and the private difference was resolved (displays differ by at least 0.001), public got the private sign right 11 times, wrong 3 times and showed no difference 3 times. The offline labs got it right 6 times and wrong 11 times. When the two disagreed and only one was right, public won 6 cases to 1: edge filter a0, DeepCenter 0.30, relink OFF, hygiene, axis-flip and exp03B primary against Z-flip. Public was very poor at predicting size, though. The knobs we picked from public reads (cap 6, K, CI, DIS) moved public by +0.006 from #37 to exp89t (0.954 to 0.960) and private by 0 (0.920 to 0.920). Across the 18 x138-family files at public 0.954 or higher, public and private are uncorrelated (Spearman -0.04). The one lever with held-out-video OOF support, DaughterNet insertion, is the only one that grew on private: OOF +0.0019, public +0.001, private +0.003 to +0.005. So its OOF number was the best size estimate we had, and the in-sample exp60 lab (+0.0065) overstated it about twofold. The realised world matches the audit's 'cap 6 and K worth 0 on private, and the rival forks lose too' scenario. The audit gave the pair roughly 0.72 for bronze and 0.42 for silver there. We got bronze and missed silver by 145 places. The audit's worst case, where we lose our gains and the field keeps theirs (about #541, no medal), did not happen, and #37 alone would have medalled. The edge-filter lesson is confirmed and stronger than before: the private sign was negative, not just zero. 'Public-tuned knobs shrink on private' is also confirmed, and they shrank to roughly nothing. One caveat: the only public-null lever that paid on private was DeepCenter 0.20 (+0.002, our best file exp70j at 0.922), and neither predictor saw it.

lessons: Public LB reads worked as a veto: when a lever read -0.001 or worse on public, private agreed in 8 of 9 resolved cases. They did not work for choosing +0.001 to +0.002 gains near the top, where public and private are uncorrelated (Spearman -0.04, n = 18).

Only held-out OOF gave a usable size estimate: insertion OOF +0.0019 against private +0.003 to +0.005. In-sample and leaky labs (edge filter, DivNet veto, relink, hygiene, axis-flip, primary swap) had the wrong sign in 9 of 11 cases. Treat an in-sample lab as having no information on sign.
The edge-filter lesson holds and is stronger than recorded: private was -0.001 and -0.002, not 0. MEMORY's 'lab over-trusts ILP/edge-net edits' should now say 'wrong-signed on private'.

'Public-tuned knobs shrink on private' is confirmed: cap 6 + K + CI + DIS went from +0.006 public to 0 private (exp89t vs #37). A pre-registered public threshold such as decision B's >= 0.960 cannot tell a 0.001 public gain from a private loss, and DIS came out at -0.001.

The rounding rule cuts both ways. Equal displays leave the difference unresolved, but a one-step display difference does fix the sign, with the true difference in (0, 0.002). So DIS -0.001 and CI +0.001 on exp87a vs exp85a are real signs of uncertain size.

The Monte Carlo was calibrated in direction (bronze yes, silver at risk). Its lever priors were too pessimistic for cap 6 and K (about 0, not -0.001) and too low for insertion (+0.003, against a prior mean of +0.0015). Its field model was too optimistic about our public rank carrying over.

Neither predictor found the private winners: DeepCenter 0.20 (+0.002), secondary exp23 (+0.003) and secondary weight 0.5 (+0.007). This argues for spending one final slot on a diverse file rather than on the public maximum.

Next competition: build an out-of-embryo (or at least held-out-video, OOF) lab before tuning. Pick finals by CV-backed levers and use public only to veto. Do not climb public ladders (cap 4/6/8/12, DeepCenter 0.20/0.225/0.30).

summary: I rebuilt all 57 rows of _final_subs.csv (56 distinct files; probe 18 was submitted twice by accident, refs 56252420 and 56252506) and 59 A/B contrasts. Only one of our own levers carried over from public to private: the DaughterNet division insertion. In all three clean pairs it showed +0.001 on public and +0.005 / +0.003 / +0.003 on private, so the public embryo understated it by 3-5x. It was also the only lever with a held-out-video OOF check. The knobs we picked from public reads on the x138 base went the other way. Cap 6/8/12, K, CI (three times) and DIS summed to +0.010 on public and -0.001 on private: six show 0, CI on top of K shows +0.001, DIS shows -0.001. Public-negative contrasts behaved differently. Every one in the x138 family kept its sign (DC 0.30: -0.005/-0.002) or went to 0 (SEC -0.002 and -0.003 both went to 0). In the pre-x138 era, 5 public negatives flipped to private positives. Overall Spearman(public, private) is 0.84, but that comes from the gaps between eras and from the broken probes. Within each era it is roughly zero: 0.08 in the exp06 era, 0.03 in the TTA era, and -0.04 among the 18 insertion-bearing x138 files with DC 0.25 or lower. Over the whole x138 family the regression slope of private on public is only 0.25. The practical result: our finals (exp89t public 0.960, #37 public 0.954) both landed at 0.920, exp87a would have given 0.921, and our best private file (exp70j 0.922, from DC 0.20, a lever public showed as 0) could not be picked from public at all. It was one of 7 files tied at public 0.954.

lessons: Our bronze came from the unrounded tie-break inside the 0.920 display block (#336-#413, bronze line #402 also 0.920), so it was closer than '56 places' suggests. One display unit (exp87a's 0.921) would have moved us into the ~#288-335 zone.

The whole public-fork lineage (pilkwang -> x138) had a private ceiling of about 0.917-0.928. Every team in the write-ups that got above ~0.93 private either trained its own detector or division models, or added many learned heads validated embryo-wise on all 199 videos. Post-processing knobs picked on public reads did not transfer.

The one lever of ours with held-out-video OOF support (DaughterNet insertion, +0.003 private) is the one that carried. The public-only levers (cap 6, K, CI, DIS, SEC) summed to about +0.001 private (unresolved per lever). This matches Corwin's and the 89th's findings that detector and threshold knobs tuned on public were flat on private.

Above public 0.954 our public score had no rank information about private (Spearman -0.04, n=18). The 89th (0.06) and the 18th (r=0.09) report the same. Decisions made on +0.001 public reads were noise.

Build an honest out-of-embryo or OOF validator on day 1 with models we own. Our from-scratch detector attempt (5-21 epochs, LOEO 0.68) was abandoned too early. hjyact showed that a 100-epoch 2.5D ConvNeXt-nano, judged on an unseen embryo, reached 0.939 private.

Keep one final slot for an independently validated or different-chassis file. hjyact (0.939 vs selected 0.917) and the 89th (0.935 vs 0.928) both lost their best private file by selecting two public-favoured siblings. Both our finals were x138-family.

The private embryo was reportedly sparser than the public one and than training (yu4u's probing). Divisions and continuity transferred better there than detector-calibration tweaks did (Corwin: continuity pieces held at 1.3-3x their public size on private).
